desc:
Design an iterator over a binary search tree that walks the values in ascending order. It supports two operations:

  • next() (code 0) returns the next smallest value that has not been returned yet.
  • hasNext() (code 1) tells whether any value is left: 1 if yes, 0 if not.

You receive the tree and a list ops of operation codes. Perform them in order and return one number per operation: the returned value for next, and 1 or 0 for hasNext. A next call is only made when a value is left.

The intended solution uses only O(h) extra memory (h is the tree height) and O(1) amortized time per call, so it must not copy the whole tree into an array first.

Tree encoding. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order. The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn, level by level, from left to right. A missing child is written as -1 (node values are never negative, so -1 cannot be confused with a value). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped. The empty tree is [].

For example, [5,2,7,-1,3,6] is the tree whose root 5 has left child 2 and right child 7; node 2 has no left child and right child 3; node 7 has left child 6 and no right child.

Example

tree = [7,3,15,-1,-1,9,20], ops = [1,0,0,0,1,0,0,1,1]
Output: [1,3,7,9,1,15,20,0,0]
The values in order are 3, 7, 9, 15, 20.
constraints: 0 ≤ node value ≤ 100,000, all values distinct; the tree is a valid BST
1 ≤ ops.length ≤ 10,000; every op is 0 or 1, and op 0 is never issued when no value is left
hints: Flattening the tree into a sorted array and keeping an index is easy, but costs O(n) memory. What is the smallest part of the tree you have to remember?
Keep a stack holding the path to the next value: the current leftmost node and its ancestors that are still waiting.
On next, pop the top node (that is the answer), then push the left spine of its right child. hasNext is simply 'is the stack non-empty'.
editorial: Simulate an inorder traversal that is paused after every value. The stack always contains the nodes whose own value and right subtree are still unvisited, topmost first. Initially push the left spine from the root, so the top is the minimum.

next pops the top node, which is the smallest unreturned value, and then pushes the left spine of that node's right child so that the new top is the following value. Each node is pushed and popped once, which gives O(1) amortized time per call, while the stack never holds more than h nodes. hasNext checks whether the stack is empty.
